methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. For the original research topic, the decomposition focused on the functional requirements and timing behavior described in the text. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition focused on the module interface, combinational logic function, timing dependencies, and register updates.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Timer counts down for a given number of clock cycles.
Timer asserts a signal when the given duration has elapsed.
Down-counter asserts an output signal when the count becomes 0.
If load = 1, load the internal counter with the 10-bit data.
10-bit data represents the number of clock cycles the timer should count before timing out.
The counter can be loaded at any time, including when it is still counting and has not yet reached 0.
If load = 0, the internal counter should decrement by 1.
The output signal tc (terminal count) indicates whether the internal counter has reached 0.
Once the internal counter has reached 0, it should stay 0 (stop counting) until the counter is loaded again.
If load = 0 and the internal counter is already at 0, the internal counter should remain at 0.
The output signal 'tc' should be asserted when the internal counter reaches 0 and remain asserted until a new value is loaded into the counter.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has clk, load, data[9:0], and tc.
load controls whether data is loaded into the internal counter.
tc indicates when the counter reaches zero.
tc is asserted when the internal counter's value is zero, and de-asserted otherwise.
tc = ~(counter[9] | counter[8] | counter[7] | counter[6] | counter[5] | counter[4] | counter[3] | counter[2] | counter[1] | counter[0]).
tc generation is independent of clk and load.
clk and load influence the state of the internal counter.
The data input is loaded into the internal counter on the rising edge of clk when load is high.
When load is low, the internal counter decrements on each rising edge of clk if the counter is greater than 0.
The tc output is asserted when the internal counter is 0.
The next state of the internal counter depends on the current state of the counter, the load signal, and the data input.
The circuit is a sequential circuit with one 10-bit register to store the counter value.
The register is updated on the positive edge of clk.
The counter stops decrementing once it reaches 0 and remains at 0 until a new value is loaded.
The tc signal remains asserted until a new value is loaded.
